documents.title: H&P - Admission - Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
lines: CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Shortness of breath x 4 days, worse lying flat.
HPI:
65 yo F with known HFrEF (EF 35% by echo 8 months ago), HTN, paroxysmal AF, presents to ED with progressive dyspnea.
Onset of exertional dyspnea 4 days ago, now dyspneic at rest. Sleeping in recliner, 3 pillows (baseline 1).
Reports bilateral ankle swelling to mid-shin, new abdominal fullness, early satiety.
Patient reports taking extra water pills for a couple of days; weight gain of 1.5 kg by home scale.
No chest pain, no fevers, no cough productive of sputum. No hemoptysis.
Admits to canned soup and deli meats over the past week at family gathering.
No syncope. Occasional palpitations, brief, self-limited.
ED COURSE:
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED with modest urine output in first 2 hours.
Admitted to telemetry step-down for IV diuresis.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
HFrEF, EF 35%; HTN; paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; hyperlipidemia; osteoarthritis knees.
Prior admission for volume overload approx 1 yr ago.
HOME MEDICATIONS:
Furosemide 40 mg PO daily
Carvedilol 6.25 mg PO BID
Sacubitril-valsartan 24/26 mg PO BID
Spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily
Apixaban 5 mg PO BID
Atorvastatin 40 mg PO nightly
Acetaminophen 500 mg PRN knees
ALLERGIES: sulfa - rash.
SOCIAL: lives with daughter, independent with ADLs, walks with cane. Never smoker. No alcohol.
FAMILY HX: father MI age 60, mother HTN.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
Positive: dyspnea, orthopnea, PND, leg swelling, fatigue, abdominal bloating.
Negative: fever, chills, chest pain, melena, dysuria, focal weakness.
EXAM:
Vitals 09:40: T 36.7, HR 104 irregular, BP 148/86, RR 26, SpO2 91% on 4L NC.
Gen: elderly female, sitting upright, mild accessory muscle use, speaking in short sentences.
HEENT: JVD to angle of jaw at 45 degrees.
Cardiac: irregularly irregular, S3 present, no murmur appreciated, PMI displaced.
Lungs: bibasilar crackles to mid lung fields bilaterally, no wheeze.
Abd: soft, mild RUQ fullness, liver edge palpable 2 cm below costal margin.
Ext: 2+ pitting edema to mid-shin bilaterally, warm, pulses intact.
Neuro: alert, oriented x3, no focal deficit.
DATA:
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
Troponin 0.03 ng/mL, flat on repeat.
Na 134, K 3.8, Cl 98, bicarb 28, glucose 112.
WBC 7.2, Hgb 11.8, Plt 224.
TSH 2.1. LFTs: AST 38, ALT 30, alb 3.4.
ECG 09:25: atrial fibrillation rate 106, no acute ST changes, LVH by voltage.
Chest x-ray: diffuse bilateral interstitial opacities with cephalization and moderate bilateral effusions, increased from prior study.
ASSESSMENT:
65 yo F with acute decompensated HFrEF, likely precipitated by dietary sodium load and self-adjusted diuretic dosing.
Hypoxemic respiratory insufficiency secondary to pulmonary edema, currently supported on 4L NC.
Rate-controlled AF, on apixaban, no evidence of ACS.
PLAN:
1. IV diuresis: furosemide 80 mg IV every 12 hours. Strict I/O, daily standing weights.
2. Supplemental O2 titrate for SpO2 >92%. RT to assess.
3. Telemetry. Continue carvedilol and apixaban.
4. Hold sacubitril-valsartan for now given aggressive diuresis; reassess daily.
5. 2 g sodium diet, 1.5 L fluid restriction.
6. Repeat echo to reassess EF.
7. Daily K and Mg repletion per protocol.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 - Cardiology/Hospitalist
lines: SUBJECTIVE:
Pt reports breathing about the same as yesterday. Slept semi-upright, one episode of PND at 03:00.
Denies chest pain. Appetite poor. Frustrated that she has not urinated much.
OBJECTIVE:
T 36.5, HR 96 irregular, BP 132/78, RR 22.
Remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2, SpO2 92-93%.
Net I/O last 24h: in 1,100 mL, out 860 mL. Weight 78.4 kg, down 0.3 kg.
Exam: JVD to mid-neck, crackles at bases bilaterally, S3 persists.
Ext: 2+ edema to mid-shin, unchanged.
Labs: Na 133, K 3.4, Mg 1.8.
ASSESSMENT:
Acute decompensated HFrEF, inadequate diuretic response to intermittent bolus dosing.
PLAN:
Converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
Add metolazone 2.5 mg PO x1 this morning if output remains flat by 14:00.
KCl 40 mEq PO x2, Mg sulfate 2 g IV.
Foley deferred, using urinal/hat measurements with RN.
Continue 2 g Na diet, 1.5 L fluid restriction.
Continue carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, apixaban 5 mg BID.
Echo pending today.
O2 wean as tolerated once volume improves; RT at bedside.
Will reassess I/O at 16:00 and titrate infusion.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD4 - Hospitalist
lines: SUBJECTIVE:
Pt feels markedly better. Ambulated hallway x2 with RN yesterday evening without dyspnea.
Slept flat on one pillow overnight, no PND. Appetite improved.
OBJECTIVE:
T 36.6, HR 82 irregular, BP 118/70, RR 18, SpO2 95% on room air since HD3 14:00.
Net negative 3.9 L since admission. Weight 75.2 kg, down 3.2 kg from admission.
Urine output last 24h 2,650 mL.
Exam: JVD flat at 45 degrees. Lungs clear to mid fields, trace basilar crackles on right.
No S3 today. Trace ankle edema bilaterally.
Echo HD2: EF 30-35%, moderate MR, mildly dilated LA, no pericardial effusion.
Labs: Na 136, K 4.1, Mg 2.0, Hgb 11.5.
ASSESSMENT:
Acute decompensated HFrEF, much improved, near euvolemic. Off supplemental O2 and stable.
PLAN:
Stop furosemide infusion, transition to furosemide 40 mg IV BID today; plan PO conversion tomorrow.
Resume sacubitril-valsartan 24/26 mg PO BID this morning, monitor BP.
Continue carvedilol 6.25 mg PO BID, spironolactone 12.5 mg daily, apixaban 5 mg BID.
Continue daily weights, strict I/O, 2 g Na diet.
HF teaching started with RN - daily weights, sodium label reading, when to call.
Counseled not to self-adjust diuretic dosing at home.
PT eval for gait and endurance.
Anticipate discharge HD5 if stable on oral regimen.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
lines: Admitting diagnosis: acute decompensated heart failure with reduced EF.
Discharge diagnoses: 1) acute on chronic HFrEF, EF 30-35%; 2) paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, rate controlled; 3) HTN; 4) hyperlipidemia.
Length of stay: HD1 to HD5.
HOSPITAL COURSE:
65 yo F presented with 4 days of progressive dyspnea, orthopnea and PND.
Patient reports taking extra water pills for a couple of days; weight gain of 1.5 kg by home scale, along with recent dietary sodium load.
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%; remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2.
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL). Troponin flat, ECG showed AF without ischemic changes.
Chest x-ray: diffuse bilateral interstitial opacities with cephalization and moderate bilateral effusions, increased from prior study.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED, repeated at 80 mg IV every 12 hours; converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
Metolazone 2.5 mg x1 given HD2. Brisk diuresis followed with net negative 3.9 L by HD4.
Weaned off supplemental oxygen HD3 at 14:00, SpO2 95% on room air thereafter.
Echo HD2: EF 30-35%, moderate MR, mildly dilated LA.
Sacubitril-valsartan resumed HD4; transitioned to oral furosemide HD5 with stable exam.
Discharge weight 74.9 kg, total 3.5 kg below admission weight. Ambulated 200 ft with cane, SpO2 94% on room air.
DISCHARGE EXAM:
HR 78 irregular, BP 116/68, RR 16, SpO2 95% RA. JVP flat. Lungs clear. Trace ankle edema.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Furosemide 60 mg PO daily
Carvedilol 6.25 mg PO BID
Sacubitril-valsartan 24/26 mg PO BID
Spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily
Apixaban 5 mg PO BID
Atorvastatin 40 mg PO nightly
KCl 20 mEq PO daily
Acetaminophen 500 mg PRN knee pain
INSTRUCTIONS:
Weigh daily on same scale each morning; call if up 2 kg in 2 days or 1 kg overnight.
Do not change diuretic dose on your own - call the heart failure clinic first.
2 g sodium diet, fluid limit 1.5 L daily. Written label-reading handout given.
Return for worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, chest pain, or lightheadedness.
FOLLOW UP:
Heart failure clinic in 7 days; primary care in 2 weeks; repeat BNP and electrolytes at clinic visit.
Discharged HD5 at 13:20 to home with daughter, stable, ambulatory, on room air.
